text:
arjun: heads up, CI size gate failed on the new fused-attn kernels after yesterday's merge. saw a ~18% bump on the linux-cuda artifact

maria: ugh, I noticed the fatbin grew. any idea which object is the culprit?

lucas: buildbot attached the artifact list: buildbot: size-gate failed -> 24.2MB (limit 20MB). suspect files: runtime/attn_fused.cubin, runtime/attn_fused.ptx, libkernels.a

zara: quick hypothesis: we enabled -rdc=true for a couple of kernels to allow device-side linking and that pulls in whole-fatbins for multiple archs. nvcc is generating PTX+SASS for all gencodes.

arjun: exact nvcc flags in CI are: ``nvcc -O3 -Xptxas -v -gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 -gencode=arch=compute_86,code=sm_86 -gencode=arch=compute_90,code=sm_90 -rdc=true``

maria: we used -rdc to support device lambdas in fused kernels. can we avoid -rdc for the hot path and use explicit kernel registration instead?

lucas: other levers: strip PTX for non-primary arch with ``--ptxas-options=-v`` doesn't help. but we can emit only cubin for deployed archs by using ``-gencode=arch=compute_86,code=compute_86`` vs code=sm_86. also nvcc emits both ptx+cubin when you request ptx.

zara: also observed the repo links a static lib built with relocatable device code, so the final link pulls device code from all objects. two options: build per-arch variants in CI (separate artifacts per sm) or change to host-side indirection to avoid device linking across objects.

arjun: per-arch artifacts would increase CI storage and matrix complexity but would keep artifact size small. can we compress better? we already gzip artifacts but size gate is on uncompressed size.

maria: another approach: move big kernels into a dynamically loaded plugin (dlopen) so the main runtime stays small and plugin is optional for dedicated builds. downside: complicates packaging and private deploys.

lucas: quick debug suggestion: run ``cuobjdump --list-engines runtime/attn_fused.cubin`` and ``cuobjdump -ptx runtime/attn_fused.cubin`` to verify duplicate PTX blobs. I ran it locally, saw ptx v7.0 + multiple sm targets embedded.

buildbot: build #3467: attached /tmp/artifacts/attn_fused.cubin (24.2MB), logs at https://ci.redwood/3467/logs

zara: we should also check for embedded asm in our CUDA kernels. small inline asm invocations can force full PTX fallback for multiple archs. grep for "asm(" in kernels.

arjun: plan proposal: (1) short-term: relax size gate for a single CI run while we triage; (2) immediate mitigation: change nvcc flags in CI to emit only cubin for primary target (remove broad gencode list) and disable -rdc where possible; (3) medium-term: RFC to split big kernels into an optional runtime plugin and to add per-arch CI artifacts and a post-build strip/normalize step (use cuobjcopy to remove ptx sections we don't need); (4) long-term: evaluate clang-offload-wrapper or nvcc wrapper to produce deterministic, minimal fatbins.

maria: +1. I'll open a small PR to adjust the CI nvcc wrapper for the next job and a follow-up RFC for plugin split.

lucas: I'll add a CI job to run cuobjdump checks and fail early with a human-friendly message if fatbin contains more than X archs.

zara: can we add a lint that detects -rdc=true in the repo build flags so accidental re-enables don't happen?

arjun: yes, add a Bazel/Make rule check. maria, lucas, assign owners and I'll file the RFC.

maria: assigning myself for CI flag change and the lint.

lucas: assigning myself to cuobjdump check and artifact split experiment.

zara: I'll prototype the plugin split on a feature branch.

devops-bot: note added: issue #4126 created for RFC "runtime plugin split for large kernels"; assignees: zara, arjun

arjun: thanks. let's keep the size gate strict but add a temporary exemption window until we land mitigations. ping me if you need more compute to run diagnostics. :thumbsup:
